summary: Waiting at Piccadilly, Van Helsing explains the Count's history and his experiments in moving his own boxes. A telegram from Mina warns that the Count has hurried south from Carfax. Godalming and Quincey return, having destroyed twelve boxes at Bermondsey and Mile End. They ambush the Count when he enters with a key; Harker slashes at him with his kukri, cutting his coat and spilling banknotes and gold; the Count is repelled by crucifix and Wafer and leaps through the window. He escapes via the stable, leaving a sneering threat. Van Helsing burns his remaining effects and keeps the deeds. Back at the asylum Mina asks the men to pity the Count. During the night Mina asks Van Helsing to hypnotise her before dawn, and in trance she hears water, a chain and a capstan, revealing the Count is aboard a ship. Van Helsing deduces escape and warns that, because of the mark, time favours the immortal Count.

scenes.title: Van Helsing on the Count's nature
scenes.summary: Van Helsing explains the Count was soldier, statesman and alchemist, a child-brain growing, now experimenting, including moving boxes himself.
scenes.key_quote: He dared even to attend the Scholomance, and there was no branch of knowledge of his time that he did not essay.

scenes.title: Mina's telegram
scenes.summary: Telegraph boy delivers a warning that the Count left Carfax at 12:45 for the south.
scenes.key_quote: Look out for D. He has just now, 12:45, come from Carfax hurriedly and hastened towards the South.

scenes.title: Godalming and Quincey return
scenes.summary: Both lairs found, six boxes in each destroyed.
scenes.key_quote: We found both places; six boxes in each and we destroyed them all!

scenes.title: The ambush
scenes.summary: Quincey positions the party; the Count bounds in, Harker's kukri cuts his coat spilling money, crucifix and Wafer drive him back, he dives through the window and escapes via the stable.
scenes.key_quote: There was something so panther-like in the movement—something so unhuman

scenes.title: The Count's threat
scenes.summary: He taunts them and bolts the stable door behind him, vanishing.
scenes.key_quote: My revenge is just begun! I spread it over centuries, and time is on my side.

scenes.title: Clearing the house
scenes.summary: Van Helsing pockets the remaining money, takes the title deeds and burns the rest in the fireplace.
scenes.key_quote: swept the remaining things into the open fireplace, where he set fire to them with a match.

scenes.title: Mina's plea for pity
scenes.summary: Over supper Mina asks them to be pitiful to the Count's soul; Jonathan, in rage, wishes his soul in hell; she rebukes him tenderly.
scenes.key_quote: it is not a work of hate. That poor soul who has wrought all this misery is the saddest case of all.

scenes.title: Night watch
scenes.summary: Van Helsing fixes the room and places a bell; the men take watches, Quincey lying on a mattress outside the door.
scenes.key_quote: One of us will be here all night. We don’t mean to take any chances!

scenes.title: Hypnotic trance
scenes.summary: Mina asks to be hypnotised. In trance at sunrise she reports darkness, lapping water, men stamping overhead, a chain and capstan; she is on a ship.
scenes.key_quote: The lapping of water. It is gurgling by, and little waves leap. I can hear them on the outside.

scenes.title: The deduction
scenes.summary: Van Helsing concludes the Count has taken his last box aboard a ship; he warns Mina that the Count can wait centuries while she is mortal.
scenes.key_quote: he can live for centuries, and you are but mortal woman.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count in life was soldier, statesman and alchemist who attended the Scholomance
vampire_lore.detail: His brain survived death and grows; memory incomplete; child-brain.
vampire_lore.quote: in him the brain powers survived the physical death; though it would seem that memory was not all complete.

vampire_lore.rule: A vampire must be invited the first time
vampire_lore.detail: After the first invitation he may come when and how he will.
vampire_lore.quote: must at the first make entry only when asked thereto by an inmate.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count learns by experiment, moves boxes himself, scatters graves
vampire_lore.detail: Initially others moved them; now he moves alone and may bury them.
vampire_lore.quote: he try to move them all alone.

vampire_lore.rule: By day before sunset the Count may not change form
vampire_lore.detail: Till sunset he is limited to man's powers.
vampire_lore.quote: till sunset he may not change.

vampire_lore.rule: He can cross running water only at slack or full tide
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing deduces he crossed the river at slack tide; a ship must touch land at tide.
vampire_lore.quote: he could only do so at slack of tide

vampire_lore.rule: Holy symbols repel in a shared gesture
vampire_lore.detail: Holding Crucifix and Wafer sends a mighty power along the arm and makes him cower.
vampire_lore.quote: I felt a mighty power fly along my arm

vampire_lore.rule: A bitten victim sees through his senses in trance
vampire_lore.detail: Under hypnosis Mina perceives the ship around the Count; strongest at sunrise.
vampire_lore.quote: I do not know. Sleep has no place it can call its own.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire is helpless at the moment of daylight transit
vampire_lore.detail: The Count is 'still' like death in his box aboard ship (Mina's trance) as the sun rises.
vampire_lore.quote: I am still—oh, so still. It is like death!

vampire_lore.detail: The kukri would have cut through his heart had he not leaped back; its effect is untested.
vampire_lore.quote: A second less and the trenchant blade had shorne through his heart.

puzzles.name: Predict the Count's arrival
puzzles.setup: Telegram says he left Carfax at 12:45 for the south.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing reasons he crossed at slack tide, visited Bermondsey then Mile End, so arrives later; Godalming and Quincey return first.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction puzzle with a London map, tide table and timeline.
puzzles.quote: he went south from Carfax, that means he went to cross the river, and he could only do so at slack of tide

puzzles.name: Ambush positioning
puzzles.setup: The Count will enter by the hall door with a key.
puzzles.obstacle: Seat the party so he cannot get past.
puzzles.book_solution: Quincey places Van Helsing, Harker and Seward behind the door; Godalming behind and Quincey in front near the window.
puzzles.game_idea: Grid placement puzzle for an ambush.
puzzles.quote: Quincey Morris had always been the one to arrange the plan of action

puzzles.name: Hypnotic reading of the Count's surroundings
puzzles.setup: Mina in trance at sunrise answers questions.
puzzles.obstacle: Interpret sounds into location and vehicle.
puzzles.book_solution: Lapping water, tread overhead, chain, capstan imply a ship weighing anchor.
puzzles.game_idea: Audio-clue puzzle: identify the vessel type from ambient sounds.
puzzles.quote: The sound of men stamping overhead as they run about. There is the creaking of a chain, and the loud tinkle as the check of the capstan falls into the rachet.

puzzles.name: Why did he take the money
puzzles.setup: Count grabs gold as he flees.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing concludes he plans to escape by ship.

combat.name: Ambush at Piccadilly
combat.tactics: Party hidden behind door and window; Count leaps past the first line; Harker blocks the front-room door and slashes; holy symbols repel; Count dives through the window.
combat.outcome: Count escapes unhurt, his coat slit and money spilled.
combat.game_idea: Turn-based ambush: positioning phase then reaction attacks; the Count has a Flee action when Holy Resolve reaches a threshold; kukri strike has a chance to cut through unless he dodges.
combat.quote: A second less and the trenchant blade had shorne through his heart.
